{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the tail, the stretch of the fish that carries the run from the end of the top line down the right side. It is the most curved and fiddly part of the picture, and it gives the fish its recognizable tail fin. I laid it from the top line's end and kept it flowing smoothly. By our last check the whole run was connected, 126 of 126 dominoes by eye, so the push had the best chance of carrying through the full outline.

Execution: I laid the tail steadily over several minutes, working carefully through the tight bend where the top line meets the tail. I raised that bend early so the table could decide whether it needed rounding. When Priya's line came up to meet mine, I stopped and let her close the last stretch, so we didn't double-lay or knock each other's work. After that I closely inspected the right side, the most likely place for a break, before the hands-off call.

Collaboration: I split the work clearly: I kept the tail as one stroke, Priya took the lower curve, and Maya handled joints. I asked for specific help rather than general help. I confirmed handoffs out loud and coordinated the meeting point with Priya so the two ends joined cleanly. I also kept my hands off once we agreed to stand clear before the push.

Leadership: I took ownership of the tail from the start and kept the table informed about where I was and when I was holding. I gave Maya and Priya concrete tasks that fit the way the work was unfolding. I also helped enforce the hands-off discipline at the end, which protected the finished run from bumps.", "my_share_percent": 30}
